children: In case there was still any doubt about whether Anthropic would plow ahead with its mega-initial public offering, a new report offers the firmest timeline yet for when the party is getting started.

Formal marketing for the offering, known as a "roadshow," could start as soon as the week of Nov. 9, Bloomberg reported Thursday. A roadshow is when a company pitches its offering to potential investors to generate excitement and drum up preorders. If the timeline reported by Bloomberg proves correct, that would put Anthropic's offering on track for a pre-Thanksgiving debut.
Anthropic didn't reply to Barron's request for comment.

The timing is key, because investors are carefully gauging whether mounting concerns about artificial intelligence will derail the AI-driven market surge that has seen stocks of Micron, Nvidia, and others reach stratospheric market values. Any further delay, such as when OpenAI shelved its own public offering this year with CEO Sam Altman calling a 2026 IPO "ill-advised," would bode poorly.

The Anthropic IPO isn't just any public offering, either. It is expected to put the company's valuation at $2 trillion and raise some $100 billion-a third more than SpaceX's June IPO. As such, it isn't just a weather vane for the market's appetite for AI stocks, but also for the IPO market as a whole.
"After a disappointing start to the fall IPO season, Anthropic would be a major test of investor appetite for high-growth, VC-backed tech," Matthew Kennedy at Renaissance Capital said.

A string of recently-shelved IPOs-most recently for smart ring maker Oura-shows how shaky the market for them is at the moment. Of course, it's also possible that investors are just holding out for Anthropic's debut. The Bloomberg report suggests that it's still on deck, never mind the haters.
